## Check your understanding

Hands-on exercises are grouped in the [Text data collection](../exercises-text-data.qmd#text-data), under **Practice**. This page belongs to that section and keeps the self-check questions below; it is not part of the main learning path.

1. An embedding matrix has $V$ rows and vectors of dimension $d$. How many parameters does it contain, and what does ID $i$ select?

<details>
<summary>Show the reasoning</summary>

The matrix contains $V\times d$ parameters. ID $i$ selects row $E_{i,:}$; its integer value is an index, not a semantic coordinate. Positional processing and contextualization happen afterwards, depending on the architecture (see the two dedicated lessons).

</details>

2. A 2D projection shows two clearly separated point clusters. Does this prove that the model correctly distinguishes these categories on new data?

<details>
<summary>Show the reasoning</summary>

No. A 2D projection preserves only selected aspects of the geometry and may create or exaggerate visual separation. Define a task, metric, and evaluation protocol on relevant held-out data; an exploratory plot is not evidence of predictive performance.

</details>

**You have understood this step if** you can explain that an ID selects a table row, distinguish the row index from the stored vector, and separate the initial vector from contextualized states.
